before: @media print supplies styles for printed output or print preview. A screen toolbar can be useful on screen but waste space on paper. Keep the report itself in the document and hide only screen-only controls in print.

The media type print is not a narrow viewport query. display: none inside this print branch removes the toolbar’s print layout space; outside print, its ordinary rule remains. Explicit dark text and an uncolored background can improve legibility, but exact page breaks, margins, color reproduction and printer settings still vary. This lesson is a local companion: the app does not render or grade print output.
Save the complete local page and stylesheet below, open the HTML in a browser, and compare the normal page with Print Preview. No printing or purchase is needed.
after: `@media print` applies styles to printing and Print Preview. You can hide page controls while keeping the report itself visible.
A narrow window does not activate print rules. Print is a separate mode. Page breaks and printer settings can still affect the result.

To try it, save the supplied `index.html` and `print.css` files together. Open the HTML file in a browser, then open Print Preview. Compare the toolbar and report. You do not need to print anything. This app does not check the printed result.

before.question: Does narrowing the browser window automatically activate @media print?
choices: Only if the page contains a link.
No; print is a media type, not a viewport-width condition.
Yes; every narrow viewport is print.
before.explanation: A viewport-size query and a print-medium query ask different questions.

after.question: Does making the browser window narrower activate @media print?
choices: Only if the page has a link
No, print is a mode, not a width
Yes, every narrow window uses print rules
after.explanation: Print rules apply to printing or Print Preview. Width rules check the available width.
